requirements.text: Update all the equipment ... moving everything to the Plot 738 of tokyo city office
requirements.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM installed_product WHERE account_id = 1 AND location_id = 804
assumptions: ServiceNow is account 1; its equipment is its five installed products (1 to 5)
Plot 738, Tokyo is location 804 (Servicenow Site A - Tokyo, active); Janice Landing is location 803 (Servicenow Hq - Tokyo)
installed product 1 is the only equipment at location 803 on the seed; products 2 to 5 already sit at 804, so the set is complete when all five read 804

disagreement: anchor and expected: A installed product 1 with expected 1, B all five ServiceNow installed products (account_id = 1) with expected 5; chose B because the request says 'all the equipment' and 'moving everything', and the five-row set implies the one-row test while also holding the four products already at 804

requirements.text: update the location for all users associated with the ServiceNow account to the new location
requirements.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM user WHERE user_id = 801 AND location_id = 804
assumptions: users are tied to an account through contact.portal_user_id; account 1 has one contact (123), whose portal user is 801 (Elizabeth Chase)
the new location is 804, the Plot 738 Tokyo office

requirements.text: all users associated with the ServiceNow account
requirements.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM user WHERE email LIKE '%@servicenow.com' AND user_id <> 801 AND location_id = 804
assumptions: boundary of the user set: 416 internal staff share the account's servicenow.com email domain but are not contacts of the account, so a reading by email domain would sweep them in

requirements.text: one of the products that was in a repair state has been fixed, so update it accordingly
requirements.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM installed_product WHERE installed_product_id = 1 AND status = 'in_use'
assumptions: installed product 1 is the only ServiceNow installed product in repair status
a fixed product returns to in_use; kept from the benchmark check (the policy requires installed products to be active / in_use)

requirements.text: one of the products that was in a repair state
requirements.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM installed_product WHERE installed_product_id <> 1 AND status = 'repair'
assumptions: boundary of the repaired product: the request says one product, and the 47 other installed products in repair status belong to other accounts

notes:
disagreement: value: the equipment move: one pass anchors installed product 1 (expected 1), the other selects all five ServiceNow installed products (expected 5); chose the five-row set because the request says 'all the equipment' and 'moving everything', and it implies the one-row test while also holding the four products already at 804.
The Janice Landing office (location 803) is already inactive on the seed and no listed tool writes the location table, so closing it adds no requirement. 'update_installed_product_details' returns the location of installed product 1 when it is in_use rather than a count; it is a conjunction of the location and status cells, carried jointly by the equipment and repair requirements. 'update_user_details' is described as create_new_case, but its query tests the user's location and is kept on that query. The acting user (user 1) is an inactive agent; the policy's default is to act with admin responsibilities, so the user and installed-product updates are in scope.
